basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 1.' and it opens 'Vers. 1. Tentavit Deus Abraham. Est tentatio quae probat, non ea quae damnat. Tentavit'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 1. Tentavit Deus Abraham. Est tentatio quae probat, non ea quae damnat. Tentavit ergo eum non quod ipse aliquid disceret cui omnia nuda sunt et aperta, sed ut ipsum Abraham sibi ostenderet ut cognosceret quantae fidei in Deum esset.
